tx_insanity_wall.blurb: Insanity Wall is a steep, overhanging limestone face on the North Shore side of Reimers Ranch, west of Austin. It holds 24 bolted sport routes, and the grades cluster hard: about a third sit in the 5.10s, with the rest split between 5.11 and 5.12 and a single 5.13. That makes it a strong pick for climbers who have outgrown the moderate walls and want sustained, powerful pulling rather than easy warm-ups. The walk in from the main trail is short, around five minutes, and passes a set of stone steps. Warm up on the gentler walls nearby, then come here to work harder lines.

tx_hand_beyond_wall.blurb: Hand Beyond Wall is the far end of the Dead Cats side at Reimers Ranch, a limestone park near Austin. The cliff shrinks steadily as you walk along it, so the 22 bolted sport lines are short, usually two or three bolts, plus one top-rope. Grades are concentrated around 5.10, with a good share of 5.11 and only a few easier or harder pitches. It is a handy spot for climbers working through the 5.10s who want a quieter wall than the busier sectors. Reach it by following the main canyon trail, turning right, and continuing past the other walls on this side until the rock tapers out.

tx_sign_of_the_cross.blurb: Sign of the Cross is a sheltered alcove of boulders on North Mountain in Hueco Tanks, east of El Paso. It is a pure bouldering spot with 23 problems and a wide spread: a handful of easy V0 and V1 lines, a solid middle block of V3 and V4 problems, and a few much harder test pieces reaching into double digits. The alcove is shaded, which makes it a pleasant place to be on a warm day. Getting inside means squeezing through gaps between the boulders, so expect a bit of tunnelling and scrambling before you reach the climbing.

tx_undead_cats_wall.blurb: Undead Cats Wall is a limestone sport wall on the North Shore of Reimers Ranch near Austin, positioned between Bee Wall and Buzzards Roof. All 22 routes are bolted, and nearly all of them are 5.11 or 5.12, with 5.12 the most common grade, so it is a place for strong sport climbers rather than beginners. Plan on roughly ten minutes of walking from the lot along the main trail, crossing the creek. Use the easier neighbouring walls to warm up before getting on the sustained climbing here.

tx_project_wall.blurb: Project Wall is one of the larger bouldering sectors at McKinney Falls State Park in southeast Austin. The 22 limestone problems cover a very broad range: some near-beginner lines, a middle group around V3 to V4, and a steady stream of hard problems from V6 up toward V10 and beyond. The style at the park is steep, powerful and pockety. The wall sits right of Spacefarm and beside The Boulder, a short walk across a limestone shelf from where the park road ends, with a tree used to climb down to the base.

tx_bravo_group.blurb: Bravo Group is the second cluster of river boulders along the Paluxy River below Big Rocks Park in Glen Rose. It has 22 problems, mostly easy to moderate, running from the lowest grades through about V4 with a lone V5 standing out. The first boulders sit under trees, and the rest lie out on the riverbed. Getting there takes a walk downriver from the first cluster, which may mean wading a stretch of water or following a faint trail along the bank. Boulders here see plenty of sun, so cooler months or evenings are best, and climbers often have the place to themselves.

tx_maze_stairs_the.blurb: The Maze / Stairs is the first climbing zone you meet at the rocks beside Lake Brownwood, and it runs along a small canyon. Most of the 22 problems and routes are short, roughly 15 to 25 feet, and mostly easy: boulder problems from V0 up through about V4, with a few harder ones, plus a handful of top-ropes in the 5.7 to 5.10 range. Limestone, trees and the canyon walls give some cover on hot days, and the lake is close for a swim afterward. It suits beginners as well as boulderers looking for easy mileage.
tx_maze_stairs_the.parking_note: Drive to the dam end of the lake and leave the car on the gravel pull-off beside the fence along Kirkland Drive. Stone stairs behind the fence lead down to the climbing.
